text:
Carmen L: Heads up — eng-platform is proposing we stop shipping the SDK-side observability adapter and move to a small sidecar process that centralizes telemetry for all SDKs. Need SDK owners + devex + console folks to coordinate migration and rollout.

Ajay S: Breaking surface? Python/TS/Go all impacted?

Maria P: Short answer: yes, all official client libs call into an in-process adapter (observability.Adapter.emit(...)). New plan: SDKs will POST to a local sidecar endpoint (http://localhost:8008/telemetry) or use a unix socket for on-prem. We provide a tiny compatibility shim on the sidecar for legacy payloads.

Carmen L: Key concerns to cover: quota attribution, dashboard mapping, rollout UX (opt-in flag -> deprecate -> default), and streaming support. Also want minimal friction for Hosted customers.

Ajay S: How will quotas be attributed? If telemetry now comes from a sidecar host, we might lose sdk-level labels. Need to preserve client headers (X-Redwood-Client, X-Redwood-Route) and any route metadata.

Maria P: Sidecar will forward original headers to the telemetry backend and add a telemetry-version header. We'll normalize mappings in the console (adapter.name -> sidecar.instance). For quota we plan to keep using sdk.client_id and route tags. We need SDKs to attach those headers when talking to sidecar.

Carmen L: Migration proposal:
- Phase 1 (2 weeks): opt-in via ENV REDWOOD_OBS=sidecar or SDK constructor flag observability='sidecar'. SDKs emit a deprecation log if legacy adapter is used.
- Phase 2 (8 weeks): change default to sidecar, keep /v1/legacy-metrics endpoint on sidecar for 2 months.
- Phase 3: remove legacy adapter in SDK v2.0.

Ajay S: Need exact compatibility contract. Example header preservation and sample payloads pls. Also streaming: if SDK streams tokens, sidecar needs a streaming path or a pipe mechanism. Otherwise we'll break chat clients.

Maria P: Agreed. We'll spec two endpoints: /telemetry (batch POST) and /stream (HTTP/2 chunked or unix-socket stream). We'll publish the spec today.

Carmen L: Devex note — we'll prepare a migration doc and FAQs. Want to include code snippets for Python + TS showing how to opt into sidecar.

Carmen L: Python snippet (concept):
```py
from redwood_sdk import Redwood
client = Redwood(observability='sidecar')
# env: REDWOOD_OBS=sidecar
```

Carmen L: TS snippet (concept):
```ts
import {Redwood} from '@redwood/sdk'
const client = new Redwood({ observability: 'sidecar' })
```

Ajay S: Can we add a runtime warning when legacy adapter is used so CI surfaces migration? Like a single-line deprecation logged once per process.

Carmen L: Yes, plan is: SDK prints one-time warn to stderr and emits a telemetry event called sdk.observability.deprecation_notice. We'll include a stack sample.

buildbot: ci-bot: go-sdk telemetry_adapter_test.go failed: 
 - TestHeaderPassthrough
 - TestStreamFallback
 - TestLegacyPayloadCompatibility
Full log: https://ci/internal/6182/records/789

Ajay S: saw the CI link, thanks. I'm going to triage Go tests after lunch — likely need the shim for streaming in the Go SDK.

Maria P: Action items: 
- eng-platform: publish sidecar spec + sample server (EOD) (owner: Maria)
- devex: draft migration guide, examples, console doc (owner: Carmen)
- SDK owners: add opt-in flag + one-time deprecation log + header passthrough (owners: Ajay for Go, Carmen for Py, TBD for TS)
- console: prepare dashboard mapping change and a migration event to re-attribute historical telemetry (owner: analytics team, cc @maria)

Carmen L: Timeline check: opt-in PRs in next 2 weeks, sidecar images & spec out, default flip 8 weeks after opt-in. Is that realistic?

Maria P: Yes that's our proposed timeline. If we hit major regressions we'll extend the opt-in window.

Ajay S: fine — I'll put up PRs that add the flag + warns. Will also add a compatibility test that points at a local fake sidecar.

Carmen L: sgtm :thumbsup: I'll start the migration doc and list customer impact notes (Dedicated/private might prefer unix socket).

Maria P: I'll post the sidecar spec link here once published. Expect JSON schema, stream examples, and header contract.

Carmen L: Thanks all. If anyone sees breaking CI failures, ping me in thread.
